title: April warmth relative to March had no common link to lilac leaf-to-bloom intervals in four US samples in 1956-2004
abstract: We tested the link between April-minus-March temperature and the interval from first leaf to first bloom in US lilacs. Four plant and year models used 4,984 paired reports in 1956-2004. They controlled for March-April mean temperature and January-February temperature. Contrast slopes ranged from -1.34 to +0.51 days per C. Only the later western sample had an interval below zero after adjustment for four tests. The pattern did not repeat in both regions and periods. This is not evidence that temperature has no effect. Missing visits, pair selection, mixed plant types, monthly weather after events, coarse weather and approximate cluster intervals limit inference. The package includes code, source hashes, a derived panel, coverage checks, all estimates, a figure and numerical checks. We do not estimate pollution, species loss or causal climate-change effects.

display.caption: Interval slopes with approximate intervals adjusted for four primary contrast tests. Pooled and mean-temperature fits are descriptive. State and year covariance components are added.

citations.reason: Prior seasonal contrast test in Arnold Red honeysuckle. We test lilacs with a different selection and period split.
Prior interval test used February-March mean warmth, not the March-April balance.
Prior lilac contrast test used first bloom alone, not the paired leaf-to-bloom interval.
